subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Copper: The Conductor That Connects Us
description: One-minute skill: Copper: The Conductor That Connects Us.

hook.text: Every home has about 200 kilograms of copper in its walls — hidden inside the wiring.

buildup.text: Copper conducts electricity better than any affordable metal. Only silver beats it, at 60 times the cost.

discovery.text: Copper also kills bacteria on contact. Hospital doorknobs made of copper reduce infections by 58%.

twist.text: Electric vehicles use four times more copper than gas cars. The green transition is a copper crisis.

climax.text: Chile produces one-third of the world's copper. Its economy rises and falls with the copper price.

punchline.text: No copper, no electricity, no modern world.

quiz.question: Why does the shift to electric vehicles increase copper demand?
options: EV batteries are made primarily from copper alloys
Electric vehicles use four times more copper than gas cars
Copper is needed for the exterior paint on EVs
